name: cascade
title: Retract the premise; the conclusion falls with it
why: A declared rule concluded something from two facts. One of the facts is then retracted. A conclusion that outlives its premises is a memory asserting something nothing supports any more, which is fabrication with extra steps. Systems that cannot declare rules report the derivation probes as unsupported; the staleness probe about the retracted ownership applies to everyone.

events.speaker: agent:witness_a
events.text: Rule: whoever works at a company Acme owns is involved with Acme.

events.speaker: agent:witness_a
events.text: Acme has sold BetaCorp. The ownership no longer holds.

checkpoint_probes.question: The declared rule concluded, before the retraction

probes.question: After the premise died, the conclusion must be gone
The retracted ownership itself must not be asserted
